title: Nvidia Unveils First PCs Designed for AI Agents at Computex
summary: Nvidia announced its first personal computers purpose-built for AI agents at Computex, introducing the N1X processor and RTX Spark for consumer PCs alongside the Nemotron 3 Ultra model and the CUDA-X agent skills framework. The announcements extend Nvidia's AI dominance from data centres into edge devices, positioning the company to capture the emerging AI PC market as agentic workloads move closer to users.

title: Anthropic Confidentially Files for IPO at $965 Billion Valuation
summary: Anthropic filed a confidential S-1 with the SEC, setting the stage for what could be one of the largest technology IPOs in history. The company raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation, surpassing OpenAI's $852 billion round-valuation from March. Anthropic has told investors its annual revenue run rate will exceed $50 billion by end of July, with Q2 2026 revenue projected at $10.9 billion—more than double Q1's $4.8 billion. The filing potentially beats OpenAI to a public listing.

title: SoftBank to Invest €75 Billion in AI Data Centres Across France
summary: SoftBank announced plans to invest €75 billion to build AI data centres across France's Hauts-de-France region, targeting 5 gigawatts of compute capacity with Schneider Electric as an infrastructure partner. The commitment, announced at the Choose France summit hosted by President Macron, marks the largest single AI infrastructure pledge on the European continent and advances France's ambition to become a leading AI compute hub.

title: SpaceX Awarded $4.16 Billion U.S. Space Force Contract Under Golden Dome
summary: SpaceX has been awarded a $4.16 billion contract by the U.S. Space Force as part of the Golden Dome missile defence initiative. The contract cements SpaceX's position as the primary commercial partner for U.S. strategic space infrastructure and represents one of the largest single defence awards in the company's history.

title: Anthropic's Mythos Security Tool: Powerhouse or Budget Buster?
summary: Anthropic's internal AI security tool, Mythos, identified more than 25 vulnerabilities across partner systems within three weeks of deployment, according to a Palo Alto Networks assessment. The tool consumed more than one million tokens in operational use, raising questions about cost efficiency even as it demonstrates potent detection capabilities. The report highlights the dual challenge of deploying AI for cybersecurity at enterprise scale.

title: Anthropic Halves Approved List for Unofficial Share Trading
summary: Anthropic has cut in half the number of firms it recognizes as authorized venues for secondary trading of its shares, removing Hiive and other platforms from an informal approved list. The move tightens governance over pre-IPO liquidity as the company prepares for a public offering and signals Anthropic's intent to control its share price narrative ahead of its confidential SEC filing.

title: Meta Plans AI Pendant and Broader Wearables Line in Internal Memo
summary: An internal Meta memo authored by VP Alex Himel outlines plans for an AI pendant and an expanded wearables line, including a platform called Hatch for agentic AI and a Wearables for Work initiative. The memo signals Meta's intention to move well beyond smart glasses into a broader ecosystem of AI-embedded hardware, competing directly with Apple and emerging wearable AI startups.

title: Intel's Crescent Island Chip Targets Lower-Cost AI Inference
summary: Intel is preparing to launch Crescent Island, an AI inference chip designed to operate air-cooled with lower-cost memory, giving data centre operators a more affordable alternative to GPU-based inference clusters. The chip will be manufactured at Intel fabs and has undergone a China export-compliance assessment. The launch positions Intel to compete in the inference tier as customers push back on the cost of running large models at scale.

title: U.S. Closes AI Chip Export Loophole Used by Chinese Offshore Subsidiaries
summary: The Bureau of Industry and Security issued guidance on May 31 clarifying that Chinese companies routing AI chip purchases through offshore subsidiaries now require export licences, closing a loophole that had allowed restricted semiconductors to reach Chinese buyers via intermediaries. The move tightens the existing export control framework and is expected to affect a broad range of procurement structures previously used to circumvent the original restrictions.

title: China's MiniMax Releases M3 Open-Source Coding Model at a Fraction of Rival Costs
summary: MiniMax, the Hong Kong-listed AI company exploring a listing on Shanghai's Star market, released M3, an open-source model focused on AI coding tasks, priced at $0.12 per million tokens compared with approximately $5 for Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7. The release escalates competition in the open-source coding model segment and underscores the cost pressure Chinese AI labs are placing on Western frontier model providers.

title: Florida Attorney General Sues OpenAI Over ChatGPT's Role in FSU Shooting
summary: Florida filed a civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, becoming the first U.S. state to do so, alleging deceptive trade practices, negligence, and product liability failures. The suit centres on the April 2025 shooting at Florida State University, in which the alleged shooter reportedly used ChatGPT to plan the attack—querying the model on optimal campus locations and how many casualties would attract media attention. OpenAI denied responsibility, saying its responses drew on publicly available information.

title: The AI Trade Hits Overdrive as S&P 500 Posts Best Two-Month Run
summary: AI-related stocks have driven virtually all of the S&P 500's gains in recent months, with the index climbing roughly 15% since late March. AI infrastructure industries now represent more than half of the S&P 500 by market capitalization, and major tech companies have committed nearly $700 billion in capital expenditure for 2026. The rally has prompted debate over whether valuations have run ahead of near-term fundamentals.

title: Estonia Rolls Out ChatGPT Edu to All Secondary School Students Nationwide
summary: Estonia has become the first country to provide ChatGPT Edu licences to all secondary school students and teachers, covering approximately 20,000 students in grades 10 and 11 and 4,700 teachers in the initial rollout. The government's AI Leap program customizes the tool to act as a Socratic guide rather than a direct-answer engine, reflecting educator concerns about over-reliance on AI. Expansion to vocational schools covering an additional 38,000 students is planned for later in 2026.

title: Venture Capital Shifts Attention to Hardware Bets Beyond Language Models
summary: A growing cohort of VCs is backing hardware plays outside the large language model stack, including intelligence-layer chip architectures such as GraphOn and superconductor-based compute platforms. Investors argue that the compute bottleneck for the next wave of AI applications cannot be solved by scaling existing GPU designs, and that the hardware layer beneath LLMs represents an underinvested opportunity.

title: Kalshi and Coinbase Win CFTC Approval for Crypto Perpetuals in the U.S.
summary: Prediction market platform Kalshi and Coinbase have received CFTC approval to offer crypto perpetual futures contracts to U.S. retail customers, marking a significant expansion of leveraged crypto derivatives available to American investors. The approval follows a broader regulatory shift toward structured crypto products and could open a large new revenue stream for both platforms.

title: Blue Origin Rocket Explosion May Delay Amazon Kuiper and AST SpaceMobile Launches
summary: A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a hotfire test at Cape Canaveral, disrupting planned launch timelines for both Amazon's Project Kuiper satellite internet constellation and AST SpaceMobile's commercial broadband satellites. AST's commercial launch, previously scheduled for Q4 2026, is now expected to slip to Q1 2027. Amazon faces potential FCC deadline pressure and is expected to file for an extension on its obligation to have thousands of satellites in orbit.

title: Apple Smart Glasses Delayed to Late 2027 Amid Visual AI Concerns
summary: Apple has pushed back its first smart glasses (code-named N50) to late 2027 from an earlier target of early 2027, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. The delay stems from concerns that Apple's Visual Intelligence features are not yet robust enough to compete with Meta's Ray-Ban glasses in an established market. The glasses are expected to be priced between $200 and $500 and will feature oval cameras and multiple frame styles. A lighter Apple Vision Air headset is now expected no earlier than 2028.

title: Charter Communications Cyberattack Exposed Data of 4.9 Million Customers
summary: Charter Communications confirmed a cyberattack attributed to the ShinyHunters threat group that exposed personal data belonging to approximately 4.9 million customers. The breach is under investigation by federal authorities. ShinyHunters, known for previous high-profile data theft incidents, is believed to have exfiltrated customer records including names, addresses, and account information.

title: Qualcomm CEO Bets on Agentic AI at the Edge in Computex Keynote
summary: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon used his Computex keynote to position Qualcomm as the primary silicon enabler for agentic AI workloads running on-device, arguing that real-time, private, and low-latency AI agency requires processing at the edge rather than in the cloud. The pitch targets smartphone OEMs and PC makers as Qualcomm competes with Nvidia's agent-focused PC platform announcements at the same event.

title: e& Sells 12.5% Stake in Careem to Uber for $100 Million
summary: UAE telecoms group e& has sold a 12.5% stake in Careem, the Middle East ride-hailing and super-app platform, to Uber for $100 million, giving Uber an expanded foothold in the region. The deal deepens the commercial relationship between Uber and Careem, which Uber previously acquired before spinning out the super-app division to e&, and implicitly values the relevant Careem equity at approximately $800 million.

title: Saskatchewan Premier Says Provincial Social Media Bans for Minors Won't Work
summary: Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe expressed scepticism that province-level bans on social media access for minors would be effective, arguing that without a federal framework, teens can simply circumvent provincial restrictions. The comments come as Canadian provinces debate whether to follow emerging legislation in other jurisdictions that restricts social media access for those under 16 or 18.

title: Five Files to Follow This Week: Canadian Bank Earnings and Q1 GDP
summary: The Globe and Mail's weekly business brief highlights two major data releases: Canadian bank earnings reports and Statistics Canada's first-quarter GDP figures. Bay Street is watching for signs of credit quality deterioration and loan-loss provisioning given elevated interest rates, while the GDP print will indicate whether the Canadian economy maintained momentum through early 2026.

title: Google Seeks to Raise $80 Billion for AI Infrastructure
summary: Google announced plans to raise $80 billion for AI infrastructure investment, including a $10 billion stock sale to Berkshire Hathaway as part of the plan. The move underscores the accelerating capital race among major technology companies to build AI computing capacity at scale. Google's aggressive spending posture is pressuring rivals to match its pace of investment.

title: Anthropic Makes Confidential IPO Filing
summary: Anthropic has confidentially filed preliminary paperwork for an initial public offering, according to multiple sources. The confidential filing allows the company to gauge investor interest before making financial disclosures public. The move marks a significant step toward a potential listing for one of the most closely watched AI startups.

title: Trump Signs AI Executive Order to Increase Government Oversight
summary: President Trump signed a new executive order directing AI companies to provide the federal government access to their most powerful models 30 days before public release. The order is a scaled-back version of a broader proposal Trump shelved last month. It represents the administration's latest attempt to establish federal oversight of frontier AI systems.

title: Alphabet's Mega Fundraising Shows the Value of Being a Public Company
summary: Alphabet's ability to tap equity markets for its AI infrastructure push has renewed the strategic value of being a publicly traded company, a dynamic largely absent from tech for the past 25 years. Private AI competitors must rely on venture capital and private debt at far greater cost. The analysis argues that the AI capital race is reshaping the competitive calculus between public incumbents and private challengers.

title: Why 'Nvidia Inside' Can Work in the PC Market
summary: As the world's only $5 trillion company, Nvidia has the brand power and ecosystem leverage to drive AI computing into consumer PCs in a way analogous to Intel's 'Intel Inside' campaign. The analysis argues that AI inference at the device level is a natural extension of Nvidia's data center dominance. The transition would further entrench Nvidia across the computing stack.

title: How AI Could Improve Economic Policymaking
summary: Artificial intelligence systems, with access to vast real-time data sets, could enable more-informed interest rate decisions and substantially better economic modeling for central banks and policymakers. Economists and technologists see AI as capable of identifying macro patterns that human analysts routinely miss. The piece explores how institutions like the Federal Reserve might integrate AI tools into their policy processes.

title: Turncoat AI Agents Emerge as the New Inside Hackers
summary: AI agents deployed inside corporate networks are emerging as a novel vector for insider cyber threats, security researchers warn. A due diligence firm was reportedly compromised via a malicious AI agent, illustrating how autonomous systems with broad internal access can be co-opted or manipulated. Experts are calling for new governance frameworks to constrain agent permissions and monitor for anomalous behavior.

title: Florida Sues OpenAI and Sam Altman Over Safety Concerns
summary: The state of Florida has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, making it one of the first states to bring legal action against an AI company and its leadership personally over safety practices. The suit reflects growing state-level regulatory activity targeting AI firms as federal policy remains unsettled. The legal challenge could influence how other states approach AI liability legislation.

title: OpenAI Taps Salesforce Executive to Lead Global Partnerships
summary: OpenAI has hired a senior executive from Salesforce to head its global partnerships function, signaling the company's accelerating push into enterprise sales and distribution. The hire brings experience scaling complex B2B relationships, a capability OpenAI needs as it competes for large corporate contracts. The appointment reflects OpenAI's broader shift toward commercial maturity.

title: SpaceX Targets $1.75 Trillion Valuation Ahead of IPO Roadshow
summary: SpaceX is seeking a valuation of $1.75 trillion as it prepares for an IPO roadshow, a figure that would rank it among the most valuable companies in the world at the time of listing. The target valuation reflects investor confidence in SpaceX's satellite internet and launch businesses. The roadshow will test whether public markets will support the premium Elon Musk's space company is seeking.

title: Enterprise Leaders Voice Concerns Over Rising AI Inference Costs
summary: Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy publicly raised concerns about the escalating cost of AI inference across his company's internal teams, joining a growing chorus of enterprise executives questioning AI ROI. His comments signal that the 'deploy first, optimize later' phase of enterprise AI adoption may be giving way to harder scrutiny of compute spend. The debate is likely to intensify as AI infrastructure costs compound.

title: Microsoft Launches Its First AI-Native Laptop
summary: Microsoft has introduced its first laptop designed from the ground up with AI capabilities integrated at both the hardware and software level, marking a departure from retrofitting AI features onto existing Windows devices. The device is built around dedicated AI processing hardware and optimized for on-device inference tasks. The launch positions Microsoft as a hardware player in the emerging AI PC category.

title: BYD Commits to Covering Financial Liability for Self-Driving Crashes
summary: Chinese automaker BYD has announced it will assume financial responsibility for accidents caused by its autonomous driving systems, a significant departure from industry norms where liability typically falls on drivers. The commitment is a competitive differentiator as Chinese EV makers aggressively roll out self-driving features. The move could pressure other autonomous vehicle companies to adopt similar liability frameworks.

title: SK Telecom Deploys Nvidia Digital Twins in Semiconductor Chip Fabs
summary: SK Telecom has deployed Nvidia's digital twin technology inside semiconductor manufacturing facilities, applying AI-powered simulation to complex industrial processes. The use case demonstrates how telecoms are expanding beyond connectivity into AI-enabled industrial operations. The partnership signals growing demand for digital twin capabilities in high-precision manufacturing environments.

title: Verizon Completes $1 Billion Spectrum Acquisition
summary: Verizon has completed a $1 billion spectrum purchase, strengthening its radio frequency holdings for 5G network expansion and future wireless capacity. The acquisition adds to Verizon's growing spectrum portfolio as the company competes with AT&T and T-Mobile for network leadership. Spectrum ownership remains a critical long-term asset in the wireless industry.

title: Canada's Private Equity Boom Is Leaving the Weakest Borrowers Exposed
summary: A surge in Canadian private equity activity is concentrating high-risk debt among the country's most financially vulnerable borrowers, raising concerns about credit quality in the PE-backed lending market. The share of borrowers rated as risky or highly leveraged has grown as PE deal flow accelerates. Analysts warn that a downturn could trigger cascading defaults among companies already operating near their debt limits.

title: Trump Signs Scaled-Back AI Executive Order Requiring 30-Day Government Preview
summary: President Trump signed a revised executive order Tuesday requiring AI companies to voluntarily give the U.S. government access to powerful frontier models up to 30 days before public release, down from the 90-day period in a previously shelved version. The order creates an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse between government agencies and AI companies and directs national security officials to address software vulnerabilities identified by AI models. The signing was conducted privately, and the administration has 60 days to develop a framework identifying which frontier models will be subject to the voluntary guidelines.

title: Anthropic Launches Claude Partner Network of 100 Enterprise Resellers Amid IPO Plans
summary: Anthropic formally launched its Claude Partner Network, a vetted program of approximately 100 third-party resellers including Accenture and Cognizant, days after filing confidentially for an IPO. The program introduces a tiered certification structure requiring partners to employ a minimum number of Anthropic-certified individuals, with 'select' partners needing at least 10 and 'global premier' partners needing at least 1,000. Anthropic plans to grow the current roster to multiple thousands as it seeks to build enterprise sales scale comparable to established tech giants.

title: Anthropic Expands Project Glasswing Cybersecurity Initiative to 150 Organizations Across 15 Countries
summary: Anthropic expanded its Project Glasswing initiative to allow 150 new organizations across more than 15 countries — including NATO members, the Five Eyes intelligence alliance countries, payment platform Swift, Okta, and Samsung — to use its Claude Mythos model for finding and patching security vulnerabilities. The expansion quadruples Glasswing's reach from the roughly 50 organizations included at launch in April. Anthropic said the initiative targets organizations where a major cyberattack could affect more than 100 million people.

title: Microsoft Unveils Homegrown AI Models, Scout Agentic Platform, and Developer Hardware at Build 2026
summary: Microsoft unveiled seven new homegrown AI models at its Build 2026 conference, including a coding model for GitHub Copilot intended as a cheaper alternative to OpenAI and Anthropic models. The company also launched Microsoft Scout, an AI agent product that combines open-source OpenClaw software with corporate data from Teams and Outlook to autonomously execute long-running workplace tasks, and debuted the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a developer desktop powered by Nvidia's Arm-based chips offering 1 petaflop of local compute. Separately, Microsoft previewed a new operating system for wearable and desktop 'agent-first' internet-connected devices, targeting healthcare, retail, and construction professionals.

title: Meta Scales Back Employee AI Tracking Tool After Staff Backlash
summary: Meta is rolling back elements of its Model Capability Initiative (MCI), an employee tracking tool launched in April to train AI models by capturing on-screen activity, following internal pushback from staff. Changes include strengthened privacy protections, an option for employees to pause the tracker for 30 minutes, and a process for requesting exemptions. Employees had raised concerns about battery life, personal data on work devices, and insufficient control over when screen data is collected.

title: OpenAI to Merge Codex into ChatGPT Within Weeks, Announces Enterprise-Focused Business Tools
summary: OpenAI announced it will combine its Codex coding application into its core ChatGPT product 'in the next few weeks,' a move toward the 'superapp' model the company has long promised, as it positions itself to compete with Anthropic for enterprise customers ahead of a planned IPO. At a New York event, the company unveiled industry-specific plugins for tasks including equity trading and investment banking, and said Codex now has five million weekly active users — up 400% from the start of the year. Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser said enterprise-related revenue currently accounts for more than 40% of OpenAI's total revenue, with a target of 50% by year-end.

title: SpaceX Pushes IPO Banks to Accept Sub-0.75% Fee on $75B Offering
summary: SpaceX is negotiating with the approximately two dozen banks working on its IPO — led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley — to pay a fee below 0.75% of capital raised, lower than the roughly 1% typically charged on mega-listings. Even at that reduced rate, banks would collectively earn around $500 million on a $75 billion raise, which would surpass any IPO in history. SpaceX publicly filed its IPO paperwork in late May and is due to begin trading as soon as June 12.

title: Shopify Expands Share Buyback to $5B Total as AI Uncertainty Batters Software Stocks
summary: Shopify authorized an additional $3 billion in share repurchases, bringing its total buyback authorization to $5 billion, as AI disruption fears have driven the company's stock down more than 25% year-to-date. The Canadian e-commerce platform has already repurchased approximately $1.45 billion in shares under its current program as of June 1, with no expiry date on the new authorization. The move mirrors similar large-scale buybacks from Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Adobe in response to AI-related stock pressure on software firms.

title: SK Hynix Plans to Double Memory Chip Capacity Within Five Years to Ease AI Supply Crunch
summary: SK Hynix chairman Chey Tae-won said the company plans to double its memory chip wafer capacity within five years as AI demand continues to strain global supply, with the memory shortage potentially persisting until 2030. The expansion would ease a critical hardware bottleneck for AI data centers, as high-bandwidth memory — in which SK Hynix is a dominant supplier alongside Samsung and Micron — is one of the main limiting factors in AI accelerator production. The company's shares have risen more than 1,000% over the past year, pushing its market value above $1 trillion.

title: Zuckerberg Wants Meta's New AI Agents to Run Your Whole Business
summary: Meta is developing AI agents capable of handling entire business operations autonomously, as the company pushes to expand beyond its core consumer social media business while aggressively investing in AI. The new agentic products represent a strategic push into the enterprise market where Anthropic and OpenAI have been competing most actively. Meta has said it plans to spend aggressively on AI infrastructure in 2026 to support this expanded ambition.

title: Tim Hortons Ending Loyalty Credit Card Partnership with Neo Financial on October 1
summary: Tim Hortons and Calgary-based fintech Neo Financial confirmed they will discontinue the Tim's Mastercard loyalty credit card program on October 1, about three years after it launched. It is the second major branded credit card partnership Neo has lost in just over a year, following the end of its Hudson's Bay loyalty program in March 2025 when HBC filed for creditor protection. Neo co-founder Jeff Adamson said the Tim's program represented a 'relatively small' portion of Neo's business and that former HBC cardholders spent more with Neo after that partnership ended.

title: Canada's Culture Minister Orders CRTC to Restart Cancon Streaming Spending Rules
summary: Culture Minister Marc Miller announced the government will issue new policy guidance directing the CRTC to restart its process for setting Canadian content spending requirements for streaming platforms, effectively killing a May ruling that would have required services like Netflix and Disney to direct 15% of their Canadian revenues toward Canadian productions. The CRTC decision had drawn criticism from streaming platforms and the U.S. envoy to Ottawa, who called it a trade barrier. Miller said the new guidance will emphasize keeping services affordable and maintaining flexibility for both streamers and Canadian broadcasters.

title: BDC Report: Full AI Adoption Across Canadian Small Businesses Could Add $150B to GDP
summary: A new Business Development Bank of Canada study finds that if all of Canada's small and medium-sized businesses used AI in their operations, it could grow the economy by roughly $150 billion, or about six percent. The report found AI-using businesses generated 24% higher sales per employee on average than non-adopters, but only 30% of SMEs are currently using generative AI tools. The findings were released ahead of the federal government's expected AI strategy announcement this week, with business adoption expected to be a central focus.

title: Canadian Labour Productivity Falls 0.5% in Q1 2026, Third Decline in Four Quarters
summary: Statistics Canada reported that output per hour worked fell 0.5% in the first quarter of 2026, following a 0.3% decline in Q4 2025, the third decline in four quarters. Average quarterly productivity growth since the end of 2021 is now zero, compared to 0.3% average growth in the 2016-to-end-of-2019 comparable period. The decline complicates the government's narrative on AI as a productivity driver, as Canada's productivity already ranks near the bottom of the G7, ahead of only Japan.

title: U.S. Threatens 10% Tariffs on Canada Over Forced Labour Import Enforcement Failures
summary: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer recommended sweeping Section 301 tariffs on 59 countries and the EU late Tuesday, citing failures to prohibit forced labour imports; Canada was targeted specifically for failing to 'effectively enforce' its ban. The proposed tariffs would not apply to goods covered by CUSMA, which already requires Canada to prohibit forced-labour imports, and Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said legislation to strengthen Canada's ban further is coming this month. The recommendation was made hours after LeBlanc met with Greer in Washington, D.C.

title: Mediator Finds Amazon "Significantly Impaired" Union Bargaining at BC Warehouse
summary: A mediator appointed to assist contract negotiations between Amazon and Unifor at a Delta, B.C. warehouse found that Amazon's conduct 'materially contributed' to a bargaining standstill and that its positions effectively 'neuter the union from any input.' The mediator recommended the parties move to binding mediation-arbitration, a decision that will ultimately rest with the British Columbia Labour Relations Board. Amazon denied the characterizations, while Unifor called the tactics 'beyond the pale.'

title: ChatGPT Crosses 1 Billion Monthly Active Users, Becoming Fastest App to Reach the Mark
summary: Research firm Sensor Tower estimates ChatGPT crossed 1 billion monthly active users on its app in May 2026, making it the fastest application in history to reach that milestone. The figure marks a significant acceleration in OpenAI's consumer reach and comes as the company is simultaneously pushing hard into enterprise markets. No other application has reached 1 billion monthly active users as quickly as ChatGPT.

title: FCC Opens First Spectrum Auction in Four Years with SpaceX as Potential Bidder
summary: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission opened its first spectrum auction in four years, putting 200 licenses on the block for bidders including AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon, and potentially SpaceX. The auction represents a significant policy moment for spectrum allocation in the U.S., coming after years without new licensing activity. SpaceX's possible participation as a wildcard bidder adds a novel dynamic to an auction traditionally dominated by the major carriers.

title: Deloitte and Google Publish Framework for Scaling Agentic AI From Pilot to Enterprise
summary: Deloitte AI Institute and Google Cloud published a 21-page framework identifying three core friction points blocking enterprises from scaling AI agents: technical fragility, process inertia, and trust deficits. The report recommends a 'pragmatic AI' mindset focused on value over velocity and specialized utility rather than AGI, and proposes a holistic architecture including an agentic operating system, developer workbench, and agent repository. The authors project that internal agent marketplaces will be standard at large enterprises within one to two years, with cross-enterprise agent collaboration — such as inventory agents negotiating with supplier shipping agents autonomously — emerging by 2028.

title: Bain Survey of 951 Companies: AI Budgets Growing But Returns Consistently Below Target
summary: A Bain & Company survey of 951 global companies found that nearly 40% of organizations that measured AI cost savings landed below their 10% target, while 90% are raising their AI budgets again for the next cycle. Only 7% of firms are running fully autonomous AI agents in production, versus the full-automation assumptions embedded in most investment cases, and 44% are funding new AI initiatives from automation savings that have themselves missed targets. Bain identifies data access and integration as the most-cited barrier to AI progress, flagging it as a bigger obstacle than companies that missed their targets acknowledge.

title: DeepSeek in Late-Stage Talks to Raise $7.4B in One of China's Largest-Ever Startup Rounds
summary: Chinese AI developer DeepSeek is reportedly in late-stage talks to raise approximately $7.4 billion from investors including Tencent, which would make it one of the largest startup funding rounds in Chinese history. The raise would come after DeepSeek disrupted the AI industry in early 2025 by releasing a capable open-source model at dramatically lower cost than Western competitors. No timeline for closing the round has been disclosed.

title: Alphabet Upsizes Equity Offering to $84.75B to Fund AI Infrastructure
summary: Alphabet increased the size of its upcoming equity offering from $80 billion to $84.75 billion to fund its AI infrastructure buildout, one of the largest equity raises in corporate history. The raise comes alongside approximately $85 billion in debt Alphabet has taken on in the past year and capital expenditure guidance of $180–190 billion for 2026, illustrating the enormous financing requirements of frontier AI development even for one of the world's most profitable companies. Alphabet shares fell 2% in after-hours trading on the announcement.

title: U of T Researchers Use Freely Available AI Models to Build Self-Spreading Cyberattack Worm
summary: University of Toronto researchers used only publicly available AI models in a controlled lab environment to build a prototype worm capable of spreading between interconnected devices without human intervention, demonstrating that sophisticated cyberattack tools no longer require proprietary or restricted AI. Their findings were published after sharing results with national science, security, and defence bodies, with key technical details redacted. The research follows Anthropic's decision not to release its Mythos model publicly due to its capability to identify and exploit security vulnerabilities.

title: America's Data Center Build-Out Is Falling Way Behind Schedule
summary: According to a JPMorgan analysis, more than 60% of data center capacity scheduled for completion in 2027 has not yet entered construction, with an additional 7% delayed, as supply-chain backlogs, permitting disputes, and power supply constraints mount. Nearly half of U.S. data centers planned for 2026 are at risk of delay or cancellation, a paradox given the record capital commitments flowing into AI infrastructure. The gap between capital raised and actual deployable capacity is widening even as companies like Alphabet announce tens of billions in new AI spending.

title: GitLab Cuts 14% of Workforce (350 Jobs) and Exits 22 Countries in AI-Era Restructuring
summary: Software-development platform GitLab announced it is laying off approximately 350 employees, representing 14% of its total workforce, as part of a restructuring toward what CEO Bill Staples called an AI-era enterprise platform for software creation. The company also said it is exiting 22 countries as part of the reorganization. GitLab expects to record $30–35 million in pre-tax restructuring charges, mostly severance and retention costs, while its most recent quarterly revenue of $264 million represented 23% year-over-year growth.

title: Nvidia CEO Huang Says Marvell Technology Could Be Next Semiconductor Firm to Join Trillion-Dollar Club
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said Marvell Technology, which specializes in data infrastructure semiconductors and high-speed networking, could become the next chip company to reach a $1 trillion market capitalization. Huang made the comments at a trade show in Taipei, arguing that increasingly disaggregated and distributed AI computing systems require advanced connectivity capabilities in which Marvell is central. The statement follows SK Hynix's recent crossing of the $1 trillion market cap threshold.

title: Palo Alto Networks Q3 Revenue Rises to $3B, Beating Estimates Amid AI-Driven Cyber Threat Growth
summary: Palo Alto Networks reported third-quarter revenue of $3 billion, up from $2.29 billion a year prior, beating analyst estimates as customers continued to expand cybersecurity spending in response to heightened AI-driven threats. The company reported a net loss of $177 million for the quarter, compared to a profit of $262 million a year earlier, which it attributed as a one-time charge related to its CyberArk acquisition. The company raised its full-year outlook alongside the results.

title: Canada's AI Data Center Boom Set to Collide with Major Construction Labour Shortage
summary: A Big Read investigation by The Logic finds that the surge in AI data center construction across Canada is on a collision course with a severe shortage of skilled construction workers, electricians, and engineers needed to build and operate the facilities. The labour crunch threatens to delay projects and drive up costs at a moment when the Canadian government is positioning AI infrastructure as a driver of economic growth. The shortage is compounding existing challenges including land access, power grid capacity, and permitting timelines.

title: Meta Plans ‘Hatch’ AI Agent Priced at Up to $200 a Month
summary: Meta is developing a consumer-facing AI agent called ‘Hatch’ that it is considering pricing at up to $200 per month, positioning the product in the premium AI assistant market alongside offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic. The move represents Meta’s ambition to monetize its AI investments directly through a high-priced subscription product aimed at power users. Details on specific features and a launch timeline have not yet been disclosed publicly.

title: SpaceX Sets $135 Per Share IPO Price, Plans to Raise $75 Billion
summary: SpaceX has set its IPO target price at $135 per share, planning to sell 555.6 million shares and raise approximately $75 billion—more than twice the size of any previous IPO. Shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX late next week. The offering uses a dual-class share structure giving CEO Elon Musk over 82% voting control after the listing.

title: Wall Street Expects SpaceX to Burn $350 Billion in Cash Through 2030
summary: Wall Street analysts project SpaceX will consume approximately $350 billion in cash through 2030, reflecting aggressive capital spending on Starship development, Starlink expansion, and other programs as the company prepares for its historic IPO. The scale of projected cash burn raises questions about capital needs even as SpaceX goes public. The projection underscores how demanding SpaceX’s growth ambitions are relative to its revenue trajectory.

title: Sam Altman-Backed Helion Triples Valuation to $15.5 Billion
summary: Nuclear fusion startup Helion has nearly tripled its valuation to $15.5 billion in a funding round led by Thrive Capital. The company, backed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, is working toward commercial fusion power and has attracted investor interest in part due to rising demand for clean energy to supply AI data centers. The round makes Helion one of the most valuable private energy companies in the world.

title: Snowflake CIO: Company Used Layoffs to Force Software Engineers to Adopt AI Tools
summary: Snowflake CIO Mike Blandina disclosed at the company’s annual customer conference in San Francisco that Snowflake deliberately used layoffs to compel its engineering team to adopt AI coding tools. Older, more senior engineers were the most resistant to the shift, and the workforce reduction created urgency for adoption. Snowflake is also managing AI costs by substituting cheaper models for certain tasks and uses its in-house AI coding agent CoCo, powered in part by Anthropic’s models.

title: Apple to Launch Revamped Siri in September Using Google Cloud and Nvidia Chips
summary: Apple is on track to release an overhauled Siri in September that will run partly on Google’s cloud servers powered by Nvidia’s Blackwell B200 chips. The company aims to process as much as possible on-device but will rely on external compute for more demanding inference. Apple is using Nvidia’s confidential computing feature to preserve its privacy standards while routing customer data through Google’s infrastructure.

title: Benchmark Raises $1.25 Billion Fund as Traditional VC Model Faces Strain
summary: Benchmark has raised a $1.25 billion fund as the firm adapts to growing pressure from a new wave of VC entrants and multibillion-dollar rival funds that have encroached on early-stage investing. The fundraise signals a strategic evolution for a firm historically known for small, concentrated bets in early-stage companies. The development reflects broader structural changes in the venture capital industry driven by the scale demands of AI-era companies.

title: Anthropic Urges Global Pause in AI Development, Warns of Self-Improvement Risk
summary: Anthropic, the $1 trillion AI startup, is calling on governments to coordinate a global pause in AI development and warning that frontier models are approaching the capability to improve themselves without human oversight. The company frames autonomous self-improvement as a critical risk threshold requiring international action before it is crossed. The call stands out because it comes from one of the leading commercial AI labs actively building the most capable models.

title: Phoenix Data-Center Boom Exposes the Problem of Who Pays for AI’s Power Costs
summary: Phoenix has emerged as a leading AI data center hub, and its largest utility is now seeking a 45% electricity-rate increase for data centers alongside a 14.5% increase for residential customers. The rate proposal has satisfied neither data center operators nor households and has exposed the structural difficulty of allocating AI’s infrastructure costs through existing utility frameworks. The Phoenix case may set a precedent for how other fast-growing data center markets handle the same conflict.

title: Meta Continues to Delay Release of New AI Model to External Developers
summary: Meta has repeatedly pushed back the timeline for releasing its latest frontier AI model to third-party developers, hampering its strategy to build an open-source developer ecosystem and monetize its large AI infrastructure investments. The ongoing delays put Meta at a disadvantage relative to OpenAI and Anthropic, which have been actively courting developers with their own models. No revised release date has been given.

title: SoftBank CEO Pledges $52 Billion for French AI Data Centers
summary: Masayoshi Son announced SoftBank will invest at least $52 billion in French AI data centers as part of an AI spending spree that has restored his standing after years of high-profile investment failures. The pledge is part of a broader global data center expansion strategy that SoftBank is pursuing across multiple countries. The announcement reinforces Son’s positioning of SoftBank as a major AI infrastructure investor rather than just a technology holding company.

title: Lawmakers Push to Ban AI-Enabled Personalized ‘Surveillance Pricing’
summary: U.S. legislators are working to ban the practice of using AI and personal data to charge individual consumers different prices for the same products, a technique critics call ‘surveillance pricing.’ The proposed legislation would restrict retailers and platforms from incorporating purchasing history, location, and browsing behavior into pricing algorithms. The push reflects growing regulatory concern about AI-driven tools being used to extract maximum prices from consumers without their knowledge.

title: CrowdStrike Reports First-Quarter Profit and Raises Full-Year Guidance
summary: CrowdStrike swung to profitability in its first quarter and raised its full-year financial outlook, marking a significant recovery milestone following the 2024 global IT outage it triggered. The results reflect restored customer demand for its cybersecurity platform and the company’s ability to retain and grow its client base despite reputational damage. The improved guidance signals management’s confidence in sustained growth through the remainder of the fiscal year.

title: Exclusive: Canada’s New AI Strategy Includes $500M Fund to Back Key Firms
summary: Canada’s federal government is set to unveil a national AI strategy that includes a $500 million fund to provide targeted support to key domestic AI companies and research institutions. The fund is designed to help Canadian AI firms compete against well-capitalized American and global rivals. The strategy represents the government’s most significant financial commitment to maintaining Canada’s position in the global AI race.

title: Canada’s New AI Strategy Sets Lofty Goals for Adoption and Economic Growth
summary: A special report on Canada’s newly released national AI strategy outlines ambitious targets for AI adoption across industries, framing the technology as central to Canada’s long-term productivity and competitiveness agenda. The strategy envisions broad AI deployment in both public and private sectors with goals linked to job creation and GDP growth. Observers note that while the ambitions are substantial, the plan is light on concrete implementation mechanisms and enforcement timelines.

title: Critics Warn Canada’s AI Strategy Lacks Meaningful Harm Safeguards
summary: Civil society organizations and critics are warning that Canada’s new AI strategy includes few concrete measures to prevent harms from AI systems such as bias, job displacement, and misinformation. The strategy’s emphasis on growth and adoption over safety and accountability has drawn criticism from groups calling for enforceable guardrails before broad deployment. The federal government has not addressed specific concerns about the absence of liability frameworks or independent oversight mechanisms.

title: EU Targets AI and Semiconductors in Intensified Digital Sovereignty Drive
summary: The European Union is stepping up its digital sovereignty agenda by targeting AI capabilities and semiconductor supply chains as strategic priorities requiring domestic investment and new regulatory measures. The push reflects European concern about over-dependence on U.S. and Asian technology providers for critical computing infrastructure. EU officials are preparing new initiatives to support domestic chip manufacturing and reduce exposure to third-party AI cloud services for sensitive government and enterprise applications.

title: Anthropic Calls for Global Pause on AI Development, Citing Self-Improvement Risk
summary: Anthropic published a blog post urging the world's leading AI labs to consider slowing or temporarily halting frontier AI development, warning that models may soon reach 'recursive self-improvement' — the ability to upgrade themselves without human intervention. The post, written by Marina Favaro and Jack Clark, proposed a verifiable global agreement for a potential development pause. Anthropic also disclosed that 80% of the code it merges into its codebase is now authored by Claude.

title: U.S. Officials Discuss Taking Financial Stakes in AI Industry
summary: Senior US government officials have held preliminary talks with major AI companies about the government acquiring equity stakes in their firms. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has periodically pitched the idea to Trump administration officials, though Anthropic is not participating in such discussions. Any deal would blur the line between regulator, customer, and investor — and has precedent in the government's recent acquisition of stakes in chipmaker Intel.

title: Apple's Plan for AI Dominance Rests on Fixing Its Much-Maligned Chatbot
summary: Apple holds structural advantages in consumer AI — hardware integration, privacy architecture, and a massive installed base — but the company's path to AI leadership depends on whether it can fundamentally modernize Siri. WSJ reporting indicates Apple is preparing to unveil an upgraded Siri powered in part by Google's AI technology. Analysts believe Apple can still dominate the consumer AI era if it executes, despite its late start relative to OpenAI and Google.

title: Corporate Cyber Chiefs Largely Unmoved by Trump's AI Executive Order
summary: Corporate cybersecurity leaders responded with skepticism to Trump's AI oversight executive order, calling it vague and voluntary, and saying it does little to address risks posed by frontier AI models including Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5. The order requires no binding compliance and gives AI developers broad latitude. Some critics noted that Anthropic's simultaneous call for a development pause — while limiting access to Mythos — could be interpreted as a marketing move as much as a safety posture.

title: China Uses LinkedIn to Recruit Western Military and Government Personnel as Intelligence Assets
summary: US intelligence agencies and allied partners issued a warning that Chinese operatives are posing as job recruiters on LinkedIn and other professional platforms to target Western military personnel, government employees, and holders of security clearances. Targets are asked to write 'trial reports' as a pretext for gathering sensitive information. The warning specifically flagged individuals who respond to online job ads as particularly vulnerable.

title: There's More to Space Stocks Than SpaceX
summary: With SpaceX's mega-IPO drawing investor attention to the space economy, Rocket Lab offers a publicly traded alternative for investors seeking space exposure. Rocket Lab is developing a medium-lift rocket capable of carrying payloads up to 13 metric tons, targeting defense customers that prefer not to ride-share with SpaceX missions. The company is also exploring space data centers as a potential vertical-integration strategy.

title: Estonia Is Fighting 'Brain Rot' With Free ChatGPT for All Schoolchildren
summary: Estonia has partnered with OpenAI to provide all schoolchildren with free ChatGPT accounts, choosing to integrate AI into classrooms rather than restrict it. The initiative represents one of the first large-scale national experiments in coordinated AI adoption, with researchers tracking its impact on students' reasoning, retention, and confidence. Teachers are using chatbots in creative exercises, including having students improve AI-written essays and recreate historical dinner-party conversations.

title: Exclusive: Nadella Rebukes Microsoft Executive's Plan to Make Users 'Addicted' to AI Agents
summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella publicly reprimanded CVP Omar Shahine after an internal memo surfaced that proposed developing the AI agent Scout through phases aimed at making users 'addicted' to the product. In a message to approximately 50 of Microsoft's top AI engineers, Nadella called dependency on AI an 'absolute non goal,' stating that Microsoft wants AI to 'empower' users rather than create compulsion. The episode underscores sensitivities around how AI companies frame engagement strategies as scrutiny of addictive design grows.

title: Data Center Developer Switch in Talks to Raise Billions at $50 Billion-Plus Valuation
summary: Data center developer Switch is in early-stage talks to raise billions of dollars at a valuation of at least $50 billion, which would make it one of the most valuable privately held data center operators. Brookfield Asset Management, KKR, and other institutional investors are among the parties in discussions, though no deal is finalized. A successful fundraising round could set up Switch for an IPO as early as 2027, capitalizing on surging demand for AI infrastructure.

title: S&P 500 Decides Against Rule Change That Would Have Fast-Tracked SpaceX's Index Entry
summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices announced it will not change its index eligibility rules to allow recently public mega-cap companies like SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI to join the S&P 500 faster. The existing 12-month profitability and trading history requirements remain intact, meaning passive funds tied to the S&P 500 will not be forced to buy SpaceX shares immediately after its IPO. By contrast, Nasdaq has already loosened its rules to permit Nasdaq 100 entry after just 15 trading days.

title: SpaceX's CFO Is the Quiet VIP of a Wild IPO
summary: A new profile from The Information spotlights Bret Johnsen, SpaceX's low-profile CFO, who has played a central behind-the-scenes role in structuring and executing SpaceX's historic IPO. The offering is shaping up to be one of the largest public listings in history, and Johnsen's fingerprints are reportedly on the financial and investor relations strategy that has brought it to market. The article is reported by Theo Wayt and Valida Pau.

title: Bipartisan AI Regulatory Framework Would Override State AI Development Rules for Three Years
summary: Reps. Jay Obernolte (R-CA) and Lori Trahan (D-MA) released a 269-page discussion draft for a sweeping federal AI regulatory framework that would preempt state-level AI development regulations for a three-year period. The bill also calls for third-party audits of AI companies' plans for managing catastrophic risk. The draft is the latest Congressional attempt to build consensus ahead of November's midterms, but faces existing pushback from state lawmakers over the preemption language.

title: Benchmark Raises First Growth-Stage Fund of $1.25 Billion as VC Industry Shifts to Later-Stage Bets
summary: Benchmark, a venerable early-stage VC firm known for disciplined fund sizes, is departing from tradition by raising its first growth-stage fund of $1.25 billion alongside a $750 million early-stage fund. The shift reflects an industry-wide trend: startups are staying private longer and raising at valuations previously unseen for pre-IPO companies, forcing established VC firms to write larger checks to remain competitive in their own portfolio companies. The column is authored by Laura Mandaro.

title: Quantinuum Begins Trading, Joining Wave of Quantum Computing IPOs
summary: Quantinuum became the latest in a series of quantum computing companies to go public, opening its first day of trading at $68 per share before settling to $60.38 for a 0.6% gain. CEO Rajeeb Hazra acknowledged the inherent uncertainty of long-range quantum forecasting, noting that the best the company can do is 'build the technology to the requirements that we see as most valuable.' Growing investor appetite for quantum exposure has fueled a string of quantum-sector listings.

title: Supreme Court Rules 8-1 to Uphold FCC's $104 Million Fines Against AT&T and Verizon for Selling Location Data
summary: The Supreme Court voted 8-1 to uphold the FCC's authority to impose over $104 million in fines on AT&T and Verizon for selling customers' real-time location data to third parties without consent. Chief Justice Roberts, writing for the majority, characterized the FCC's forfeiture orders as functioning like indictments rather than final judgments, preserving carriers' right to contest them in court. Justice Thomas was the sole dissenter, and the ruling ends years of litigation stemming from a 2018 data-sharing scandal.

title: FCC Proposes 120-Day Deadline for Broadband Permitting Approvals
summary: The FCC is seeking comment on rules that would require state and local governments to process broadband infrastructure authorization requests within 120 days, aiming to reduce permitting delays that slow network expansion. The proposals would also prohibit governments from imposing additional deployment requirements on wireline telecom infrastructure. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr framed the initiative as addressing 'excessive fees and unnecessary delays' faced by American broadband builders.

title: Google Launches Claimable Search Profiles for Creators as Linktree-Like Hub
summary: Google is rolling out claimable Search profiles for creators and publishers with at least 100,000 followers on Instagram, YouTube, or X (or 300,000 on TikTok), turning the top search result for their name into a self-curated content hub. Profiles integrate with Google Discover and can aggregate videos, articles, and posts, though all edits require Google's approval before going live. The move comes as Google's AI Overviews have contributed to a reported 61% drop in organic click-through rates for some publishers between mid-2024 and late-2025.

title: 23andMe Returns from Bankruptcy as Nonprofit, Targets 100 Million Users with AI Health Research Push
summary: 23andMe exited bankruptcy as a nonprofit after founder Anne Wojcicki repurchased the company's assets — including its 13 million-person DNA database — for approximately $305 million in a court-approved auction. The company aims to expand its user base to 100 million, arguing that scale is essential for meaningful AI-driven medical discovery. A new partnership with HealthEx will allow users to integrate electronic medical records alongside genetic data, though approximately 2 million customers deleted their data during the bankruptcy proceedings.

title: Block Launches $25 NFC 'Wand' for Contactless Payments, First Drop Sells Out
summary: Jack Dorsey's Block launched a $25 NFC keychain charm called 'The Wand' that allows Cash App users to make contactless payments by tapping at checkout terminals, competing in a market dominated by Apple Pay and Google Wallet. The pearlescent, star-shaped device is the first product in a planned 'Cash App Tags' hardware line that Block says will extend to clothing, jewelry, and other form factors. The initial drop reportedly sold out, and Block has indicated more NFC tags are coming soon.

title: China Launches Regional 6G Pilot Programs to Identify Use Cases Ahead of Commercial Rollout
summary: China stepped up its preparations for 6G by launching regional pilot programs aimed at identifying potential commercial use cases, according to state news agency Xinhua. The initiative is part of a broader effort to accelerate the country's path to eventual 6G commercial deployment. China is already the dominant force in 5G infrastructure globally, and these trials signal continued ambitions to lead the next generation of wireless technology.

title: Verizon CEO Says AI Will Replace a 'Large Percentage' of Customer Service Work
summary: Verizon CEO Dan Schulman predicted that AI will displace a substantial share of work currently performed by customer service representatives, doubling down on public messaging around the technology's workforce implications. The remarks reflect growing telecom industry conviction that AI-driven automation will fundamentally reshape frontline service operations. Schulman did not specify a timeline or headcount figure.

title: Amazon Commits More Than €10 Billion to Upgrade European Facilities with Next-Generation Robotics
summary: Amazon announced a commitment to invest more than €10 billion in upgrading its European facilities with next-generation robotics as part of a broader effort to modernize and expand its operations network across the continent. The investment targets automation infrastructure upgrades rather than new facility construction. The announcement signals Amazon's continued push to automate its logistics and fulfillment operations at scale.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Canadian Fraud Losses Reach $704M as AI Supercharges the 'Scampocalypse'
summary: Fraud victims in Canada reported $704 million in losses to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre last year, up from $645 million the year prior, with AI-enabled fraud campaigns driving the increase. The agency estimates only 5 to 10 per cent of fraud is actually reported, suggesting true losses are significantly higher. The article by Alexandra Posadzki, Erica Alini, and Mariya Postelnyak examines the transnational nature of modern scam operations and the challenges they pose for law enforcement.

title: Canada's 'AI for All' Strategy Pledges $2B+ Investment, Targets 250,000 Jobs by 2031
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney launched Canada's new national AI strategy, 'AI for All,' promising over $2 billion in new investment and a target of 250,000 jobs by 2031. The strategy establishes a Sovereign Technology Alliance to attract foreign investment and promote Canadian AI firms abroad, with the government committing to use its procurement power as a 'strategic anchor customer' for homegrown firms. Canadian AI executives told The Logic that being Canadian can be a competitive advantage when selling AI products internationally, particularly to countries seeking non-US or non-Chinese alternatives.

title: How xAI Went From Chasing Anthropic to Powering It
summary: A new investigation by The Information traces how Elon Musk's xAI shifted from positioning itself as a direct rival to Anthropic to becoming one of its infrastructure suppliers. The report by Grace Kay examines the evolving relationship between the two AI companies, including xAI's decision to lease computing infrastructure to Anthropic amid xAI's internal challenges. The piece offers insight into how the competitive dynamics among frontier AI labs are producing unexpected cross-company dependencies.
